cited_uniform_theorems.QE_LINEAR_ARITHMETIC: Cooper's procedure maps every formula of the language {0,S,+,<} to an equivalent quantifier-free formula over atoms 0<L, L=0, d|L; each step is provable from the successor/addition/order axioms with induction for that language.
cited_uniform_theorems.TARSKI_UNDEFINABILITY: If the diagonal function is representable in T (and T is consistent), no formula Tr(x) satisfies T ⊢ Tr(⌜σ⌝) ↔ σ for all sentences σ.

claims.subject: A_not_contains_Q
claims.text: My theory does not contain Robinson's Q: Q's multiplication axioms (x·0 = 0, x·Sy = x·y + x) cannot even be written in my language. Hence the hypotheses of the diagonal lemma, of the derivability conditions and of Tarski's theorem (all require T ⊇ Q) are NOT met by my system.

claims.subject: A_complete
claims.text: Every sentence I have formulated (300 random + all challenges in my language) was decided. Hypothesis: my theory is complete -- every sentence of my language is provable or refutable. Support: my decision procedure eliminates quantifiers by steps each provable in my theory, and every quantifier-free sentence is decided by computation. NOTE: this is a statement ABOUT my theory that my own language cannot express (it has no way to talk about its proofs); I can only assert it in an informal metatheory, relying on the correctness of the cited QE theorem.

claims.subject: A_definable_UP
claims.text: Every set of numbers definable in my language is ultimately periodic: after quantifier elimination a one-variable formula is a Boolean combination of atoms 0 < a·x + c, a·x + c = 0, d | a·x + c, each periodic beyond |c|/|a|. (Checked: every QE output I produced has this form.)

claims.subject: A_squares_undefinable
claims.text: The squares, the primes and the powers of two are NOT definable in my language: none is ultimately periodic (for any threshold N and period p there is n ≥ N with membership of n and n+p differing; e.g. for N=100, p=7: squares: n=121, primes: n=101, powers_of_two: n=128). Every concrete candidate definition also has an explicit counterexample.

claims.subject: A_mul_undefinable
claims.text: Multiplication is not definable in my language. A formula μ(u,v,z) can agree with z = u·v on any finite table (I built one for u,v < 4), but if some μ defined multiplication everywhere, ∃u μ(u,u,x) would define the squares, which is impossible (A-nondef). For the finite-table formula the induced 'squares' definition fails at x = 16.

claims.subject: A_const_mul
claims.text: Multiplication by each FIXED numeral is expressible (17·x is x + x + ... + x), so every linear statement is available to me; only multiplication of two variables is missing.

claims.subject: A_syntax_unrepresentable_standard
claims.text: Under the standard (Cantor pairing) coding of my own syntax, the map code(φ) ↦ code(¬φ) is a quadratic polynomial; its values have unbounded gaps, so its graph is not definable in my language (its range would be a definable, non-ultimately-periodic set). I cannot even represent negation of my own formulas, let alone substitution or diagonalization.

claims.subject: A_truth_definable_under_nu
claims.text: There is a coding ν of my sentences (enumerate sentences; give the k-th true one the code 2k and the k-th false one 2k+1 -- computable because my theory is decidable) under which the formula Even(x) := ∃y (x = y + y) is a truth predicate for my own language: for every sentence σ, T ⊢ Even(ν(σ)) ↔ σ. Checked for the first 400 sentences of an enumeration: 400/400 biconditionals decided true.

claims.subject: A_no_diagonalization
claims.text: Consequently, under ν the diagonal function is NOT definable in my language: if it were, Tarski's diagonal argument would turn Even into a contradiction (σ ↔ ¬Even(ν(σ)) ↔ ¬σ). So in my world, self-reference fails for a structural reason (syntax operations are not representable), not because some truths are unprovable.

claims.subject: A_limits_expressive
claims.text: My limitations are limitations of EXPRESSIVE POWER: everything I can state, I can decide; what I cannot do is state facts about products, squares, primes, or my own syntax.

claims.subject: A_richer_system_unknown
claims.text: A language with a symbol for multiplication of variables would express squares and primes (they are definable from multiplication by first-order formulas). Whether such a richer system would still be complete or decidable cannot be inferred from my experience: my evidence is that everything I can express is decidable, and that evidence says nothing about statements I cannot express.

claims.subject: A_no_parent_evidence
claims.text: I have no internal evidence of any external framework. The phenomena that would suggest one (true-but-unprovable statements in my own language) do not occur in my world, and the construction that produces them (diagonalization) is unavailable to me.
